## Scope
### In scope
- `App\Notifications\EventCatalog` (`final`, pure PHP, no DB): every key from the plan's catalog table, e.g. `project.created`, `project.owner_acknowledged`, `project.owner_declined`, `proposal.created`, `proposal.status_changed`, `proposal.reviewer_added`, `proposal.reviewer_seen`, `proposal.on_hold_reminder`, `proposal.approved`, `project.activated`, `project.period_changed`, `project.started`, `project.ended`, `project.closed`, `project.archived`, `agreement.recorded`, `transfer.generated`, `transfer.received`, `transfer.late`, `monthly_reports.generated`, `monthly_report.due`, `.overdue`, `.submitted`, `.validated`, `.returned`, `.reopen_requested`, `.reopen_decided`, `donor_report.saved`, `.due`, `.overdue`, `.submitted`, `department_task.created`, `.due`, `.overdue`, `.delivered`, `.returned`, `program.logframe_missing`. Each entry: module, importance, direct-recipient resolver key, oversight mode (`all`, `management_only` for money events, `on_overdue_only` where the table says so), critical flag (approval, rejection, return — bypasses mutes for direct recipients), and the matching activity event or domain event class.
- `App\Enums\EventImportance` (`immediate`, `digest`) and `App\Enums\OversightMode` with `HasTranslatedLabel`.
- `App\Notifications\Recipients\OversightRecipients`: `userIdsFor(string $eventKey, ?int $cityId): list<int>`; MEAL = role holders + city officer (Task 15, fallback = whole role, D-12); management = `General Manager` + configured roles; money events → management only.
- Extend `RecipientResolver` (activity path) and `AlertDispatcher` callers (scanner path) so catalog events add oversight recipients; oversight users are non-direct (mutes apply) unless the event is critical.
- Digest importance: oversight recipients of `digest` events get them in one daily oversight summary instead of immediately (recommended: `App\Notifications\Alerts\OversightDigestScanner` in the `daily` group, counting yesterday's catalog activities per event key from `activities`; propose in plan mode). Direct recipients still get them immediately.
- Part C scanners: `App\Notifications\Alerts\ProjectDatesScanner` and `App\Notifications\Alerts\OnHoldReminderScanner` in the `daily` group of `config/notifications.php`.
- **Event Notifications** section on `resources/views/pages/admin/⚡notification-settings.blade.php`, stored through `NotificationSettings` (one key, e.g. `event_overrides`, default in `config/notifications.php` `defaults`).
- Part D: command `reports:monthly-digest {--dry-run} {--month=}` (`App\Console\Commands\SendMonthlyDigest`) scheduled in `routes/console.php` `->dailyAt('08:00')->withoutOverlapping()->onOneServer()`, exits unless today is the first working day of the month (or `--month` is given), then queues `RunScanner` for `App\Notifications\Alerts\MonthlyDigestScanner`; mail via a queued Notification `App\Notifications\MonthlyDigestMail` + `resources/views/mail/monthly-digest.blade.php` (the plan says "Mailable": a Mailable needs a new `app/Mail` folder — ask in plan mode; default to the existing Notification pattern).
- `tests/Feature/Notifications/EventCatalogCoverageTest.php`.
- Lang keys in `lang/{en,ar}/notifications.php` (`events.*` labels and messages, `alerts.project_started`, `alerts.project_ended`, `alerts.on_hold_reminder`, `digests.monthly`, `digests.oversight`, `mail.monthly_digest.*`) and `enums.php`.
### Out of scope
Writing each module's own events or activity entries (the owning tasks do it; you register keys and fix gaps found by the coverage test as follow-ups to their owners). Monthly reports (Task 17), donor reports (Task 19), department tasks (Task 31), MEAL coverage (Task 15), supervision map (Task 23). Changing the existing weekly digest, daily brief content, desktop banners or broadcasting. Attachments of any kind.

## Business rules
- **MEAL + General Management receive every catalog event** except where the catalog says otherwise (money events `transfer.*`: management only; department-task events: oversight on overdue only).
- **One notification per person**: someone who is both direct and oversight receives one (the stronger priority).
- **The actor is never notified of their own action** (existing `RecipientFilter` behaviour).
- `digest` events go to oversight recipients in the daily oversight summary, not immediately (R11); direct recipients get them immediately.
- Grouped events: `monthly_reports.generated` for 12 months at activation = **one** grouped notification, never 12 (use `NotificationGrouper`).
- Mutes (`NotificationMute`) are respected for oversight recipients; **direct** recipients of critical status events (approval, rejection, return) are never muted.
- Ledger keys include the event, the subject and the date or month, so re-runs and retries never duplicate (alerts.md).
- Working days only (`WorkingCalendar`): a date that falls on a non-working day is announced on the next working day; scanners catch up on every date since the previous working day.
- Only `active` projects get start/end notices; activation after the start date sends no start notice (Task 08's `project.activated` covers it). On-hold reminder fires once per `status_remind_on` value and only while still `on hold`. Monthly-report drafts generated for future months never alert (Task 17).
- No amounts for anyone without money permissions, in payloads, in-app text or email; the monthly digest carries counts, names and links only (no amounts for anyone).
- Settings overrides change recipients and importance without code; a disabled event sends nothing but stays in the catalog (coverage still passes).
- Monthly digest: one per user per month; a program manager sees their programs, management all; sections only when the recipient holds the module's view permission. Month rule to confirm in plan mode: on the first working day of M, month M-1 reports are not late yet (`monthly_report_due_working_days`, default 5) — show M-1 as submitted / validated / "not submitted yet (due {date})" and count earlier unsent months as missing. Default: send even when all counts are zero ("nothing pending"); confirm.
- Overlap to raise: `DeadlineCatalog::projects()` already sends a day-0 "due today" on `end_date`; `project.ended` duplicates it for the owner. Default: keep both and list it.
- Recipients are resolved from roles, module maps, HR links and settings — never from person names.

## Security and authorization
- `RecipientFilter` drops users without the module's view permission; the only exemptions are documented direct responsibles (e.g. a donor-report responsible without `funding-agreements.view`, routed to **My Reporting Duties**), passed as `exemptUserIds`.
- Oversight never bypasses the view permission: a `General Manager` or `MEAL` user without `transfers.view` gets `transfer.*` only if management-only mode allows it and the payload has no amounts.
- **Event Notifications** settings: `notification-settings.manage`, authorized inside the Livewire action, re-validated on the server.
- Emails carry absolute `route()` links to pages that keep their own auth checks, never attachments; nothing is sent from inside a web request or a transaction — notifications are queued `afterCommit`.
- Do not widen any module's watcher roles to "fix" oversight; oversight is a separate, testable layer.

## Validation
- Event settings: `events.*.key` `Rule::in(EventCatalog::keys())`; `importance` Enum(`EventImportance`); `enabled` boolean; `oversight_roles.*` must exist in the roles table (`Rule::exists('roles', 'name')`); messages in `lang/{en,ar}/notifications.php`.
- Command options: `--month` `Y-m`, not in the future, else a translated error and `self::FAILURE`; `--dry-run` flag.

## Edge cases and concurrency
- Command run twice, overlapping runs, or a retried job: `withoutOverlapping()`, `onOneServer()` and the atomic ledger claim prevent duplicates.
- Mail failure: in-app already sent; the mail job retries 3 times with backoff, then lands in `failed_jobs`; rerun with `--month` never duplicates the in-app part (separate ledger rules per channel).
- Recipient without an email in HR (`$user->email === ''`) or HR unreachable: in-app only, no exception.
- MEAL officer for the city not assigned (Task 15) or inactive in HR: fall back to the whole `MEAL` role.
- Same person as program manager and General Manager (or MEAL/PR Manager): one digest, wider scope.
- Event fired inside a transaction that rolls back: nothing sent (after-commit dispatch, tested).
- Project dates changed after a notice: new date → new stage key → announced again on its day.
- Proposal leaves `on hold` before its date: nothing sent.
- A disabled event in settings or a deleted role in overrides: ignored safely; the settings page warns.

## Data integrity
- No new tables expected: reuse `notification_alert_ledger`, `notification_settings`, `activities`. If you need a table, stop and ask.
- Ledger claim before each send; in-app and mail use separate rules so each channel is idempotent on its own.
- Catalog keys are stable strings: never rename after CP0 without both teams' approval and a plan update.
- Settings defaults live in `config/notifications.php` `defaults`; the admin page writes only overrides.

## Implementation guidance
- `php artisan make:class`, `make:enum`, `make:command SendMonthlyDigest`, `make:notification MonthlyDigestMail --markdown=mail.monthly-digest`, all `--no-interaction`; `declare(strict_types=1);`, `final` classes like the other alert classes, typed signatures, PHPDoc array shapes.
- Skeleton:
```php
final class EventCatalog
{
    /** @return array<string, array{module: string, importance: EventImportance, direct: string, oversight: OversightMode, critical: bool, activity: string|null, event: class-string|null}> */
    public static function all(): array {}

    /** @return list<string> */

    /** Merged with the admin overrides from NotificationSettings. */

}

final class OversightRecipients
{

}

final class MonthlyDigestScanner implements Scanner
{

    /** @return array<int, array{programs: list<int>, sections: array<string, array<string, int>>, links: array<string, string>}> user id => digest */
    public function preview(CarbonImmutable $month): array {}
}
```
- Build digest sections with one grouped query per section for all programs, then slice per recipient in PHP; resolve HR names in one batched lookup.
- In-app digest payload like `WeeklyDigestScanner` (`NotificationKind::Digest`, module `system`, rule `monthly_digest`, stage `YYYY-MM`, recipient exempt from the module permission). Mail: `MailMessage` with a translated subject, numbers in `dir="ltr"` spans, buttons only for routes that exist and that the recipient may open (**Monthly Reports**, **Monthly Matrix**, **Department Tasks**, **My Reporting Duties**).
- Settings section: reuse `_rules-row` patterns, Flux components, `wire:model` booleans for modals, all text through `__()`.
- After merging, record "every movement must be in EventCatalog; oversight = MEAL + General Management" with Boost `record-rule` (glob `app/Notifications/**`).

## Tests (Pest)
Follow `.ai/rules/tests.md` and `.ai/rules/alerts.md`: fixtures inside `Activity::withoutRecording`, `userWithRole()`, `$this->travelTo()`, `Notification::fake()` / `Event::fake()`, assert on the records you created.
- `tests/Feature/Notifications/EventCatalogTest.php` (Part A/B): for each catalog event (dataset), the direct recipients **and** MEAL + General Management receive it and nobody else; a dual-role user gets one; the actor gets none; money events reach management only and contain no amount for non-finance; `digest` events reach oversight only via the daily summary; a muted oversight user gets nothing while a muted direct recipient of a critical event still does; city MEAL officer vs role fallback; settings override changes recipients and importance; a disabled event sends nothing.
- `tests/Feature/Notifications/ProjectDatesScannerTest.php` and `OnHoldReminderTest.php` (Part C): start/end day for active projects only; non-working-day catch-up; second run sends nothing; changed date re-arms; on-hold reminder once per date, not after leaving `on hold`; oversight included.
- `tests/Feature/Notifications/EventNotificationsSettingsTest.php`: only `notification-settings.manage` may save (403 otherwise, fresh Livewire instance); unknown key / unknown role / invalid importance rejected.
- `tests/Feature/Notifications/MonthlyDigestTest.php` (Part D): only on the first working day (frozen dates around a weekend start of month); program manager vs management scope; one per user per month (rerun and `--month` send nothing); sections hidden without view permission; no amount or currency in params or mail; `MonthlyDigestMail` locale `ar` with Arabic body for an Arabic user; no HR email → in-app only; `--dry-run` sends and claims nothing; invalid `--month` fails.
- `tests/Feature/Notifications/EventCatalogCoverageTest.php` (Part E): every catalog key has lang keys, a direct-recipient resolver and an oversight mode; every class under `app/Events` used for domain movements maps to a catalog key; every activity event listed in a model's `activityEvents()` for projects, proposals, monthly reports, donor reports, agreements, transfers and department tasks is either in the catalog or explicitly ignored with a reason; grouped activation sends one notification.
- Extend `ScannerSchedulingTest` (command at `0 8 * * *`; new scanners in `daily`), and run `RecipientResolverTest`, `FanOutActivityTest`, `NotificationMutesTest`, `NotificationPerformanceTest`, `WeeklyDigestTest`, `DailyBriefTest`, `DeadlineCatalogTest`, `LocalizationTest`.
- Commands: `php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/Notifications/EventCatalogTest.php`, then each file / `--filter=...`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MEAL and General Management see every movement on projects, proposals and reports — immediately or in the daily oversight summary per importance.
- [ ] Program managers, management, the MEAL Manager and the PR Manager get exactly one monthly digest (email + in-app) on the first working day, in their language, with links and no amounts.
- [ ] Active projects announce their start and end days; on-hold proposals remind once on their date.
- [ ] Management can change any event's recipients or importance from **Notification Rules** without a developer.
- [ ] `EventCatalogCoverageTest` fails when a movement is added without a catalog entry; re-running any scanner or command sends nothing new.
- [ ] All listed tests pass; Pint clean.

## Do not
- Send email synchronously inside a request, or notify inside a transaction.
- Include amounts, budgets, currencies or attachments in any notification or email to someone without money permissions (and in the digest for anyone).
- Bypass `AlertDispatcher` / `AlertLedger` / `RecipientFilter`, count calendar days, use bare `startOfWeek()`, or hard-code thresholds.
- Send one notification per generated month instead of one grouped notification.
- Hard-code recipients by person name, or widen module watcher roles to fake oversight.
- Create `app/Mail`, add a dependency, add a table, or add runtime `Schema::hasTable()` guards without approval.
- Rename catalog keys after CP0.

## Working method
- Start in plan mode: confirm which part (A–E) you are implementing, restate it in 5 bullets, list files you will touch, list open questions (oversight digest mechanism, Mailable vs mail Notification, digest month rule, always-send, end-day overlap, Task 15/17/19/31 availability); wait for approval.
- Implement in small steps; after each step run the narrowest relevant tests.
- Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` after PHP changes.
- If you discover a durable rule or trap, record it with the Boost `record-rule` tool (not native memory).
- Do not commit, push, or run destructive commands (`migrate:fresh`, seeders that reset roles, deleting storage) unless the developer asks.
- Never run anything against production (B4 has no production access).
- Stay inside Task 21's scope and the requested part; note anything else as a follow-up.

Handoff facts: for every task owner — the catalog key to use and how to register a new event (CP0/CP2); for Task 26 — the event labels, settings section and email texts for the user guide; for Task 28 — how to trigger each part for UAT (`php artisan reports:monthly-digest --month=YYYY-MM --dry-run`, `notifications:scan daily` with frozen dates); for Task 29 — the new scheduled command and the queue worker requirement for mail.

Objective

«أهم فكرة هي الإشعارات اللازم توفرها عند أي حركة تخص المشروع والتقرير، بحيث فريق الـ MEAL والإدارة العامة تكون على دراية بكل ما هو لازم». تعريف كتالوج أحداث واحد، ولكل حدث مستلموه المباشرون، ومستلمون أساسيون دائمون: فريق MEAL والإدارة العامة. ثم اختبار تغطية يمنع إضافة حركة دون إشعار. ويشمل الملخص الشهري للمدراء، وإشعارات بداية المشروع ونهايته، وتذكير المقترح المعلّق.

Implementation scope

  • App\Notifications\EventCatalog: قائمة الأحداث (الجدول أدناه) بمفتاح ثابت، ووحدة، وأهمية (immediate / digest)، ومستلمين مباشرين.
  • App\Notifications\Recipients\OversightRecipients: فريق MEAL (حاملو دور MEAL، ومسؤول MEAL لمدينة المشروع من Task 15) + الإدارة العامة (General Manager، ومن تحدده الإعدادات). يُضاف تلقائيًا لكل حدث في الكتالوج ما لم يُعلَّم الحدث بغير ذلك.
  • مستلمو الأقسام: لأحداث مهام الأقسام (Task 31)، رئيس القسم وأعضاؤه من HR (EmployeeProfile::employeeIdsInDepartment).
  • قسم Event Notifications في صفحة Notification Rules القائمة: لكل حدث تفعيل/تعطيل، ونقله بين «فوري» و«ملخص يومي»، وإضافة/إزالة المستلمين الأساسيين، دون تعديل شيفرة.
  • أمر reports:monthly-digest (أول يوم عمل في الشهر، 08:00، B4): لكل مدير برنامج والإدارة، ونسخة لمدير MEAL ومدير العلاقات العامة: التقارير الشهرية (مولّدة، مرسلة، متحقق منها، ناقصة)، والمؤشرات خارج المسار، ومهام الأقسام المتأخرة، وتقارير المانح المستحقة، والمشاريع التي بدأت أو انتهت. بالبريد (Mailable مترجم حسب لغة المستلم) وإشعار داخلي.
  • ماسح يومي: «بدأ المشروع اليوم» في start_date، و«انتهى المشروع اليوم» في end_date، و«تذكير المقترح المعلّق» في status_remind_on، و«التقرير الشهري مستحق/متأخر».
  • اختبار تغطية EventCatalogCoverageTest: كل حدث في الكتالوج له إشعار ومستلمون، وكل حدث نطاق (ProposalStatusChanged، …) مطلق في الشيفرة موجود في الكتالوج.

Required deliverables

EventCatalog، OversightRecipients، توسيع RecipientResolver، قسم Event Notifications في الإعدادات، أمر الملخص + الجدولة في routes/console.php، Mailable + قالب Blade ثنائي اللغة، الماسح اليومي، EventCatalogCoverageTest، اختبارات.

Business rules

  • MEAL والإدارة العامة مستلمون أساسيون لكل حدث في الكتالوج إلا ما عُلّم صراحة (أحداث المال: الإدارة فقط).
  • لا تكرار للشخص الواحد: من هو مستلم مباشر وأساسي معًا يتلقى إشعارًا واحدًا.
  • المُحدِث لا يُشعَر بفعله (السلوك القائم).
  • الأحداث بأهمية «ملخص» تذهب للمستلمين الأساسيين في الملخص اليومي بدل الإشعار الفوري، لتجنب الفيضان (R11). المستلمون المباشرون يتلقونها فورًا.
  • مفاتيح ledger تتضمن الحدث والسجل والتاريخ/الشهر، فلا تكرار.
  • البريد والإشعار بلا مبالغ لمن لا يملك صلاحيات المال. أحداث transfer.* بلا مبالغ لغير المالية.
  • الأيام أيام عمل. حدث يقع في عطلة يُرسل أول يوم عمل بعده.
  • كتم المستخدم لوحدة (NotificationMute) يُحترم، إلا للمستلم المباشر في أحداث الحالة الحرجة (الاعتماد، الرفض، الإعادة).

Security and permissions

  • المستلمون عبر خرائط الوحدات، ولا يُشعَر إلا من يملك view على السجل (RecipientFilter)، باستثناء المسؤول المباشر الموثّق (مثل مسؤول تقرير المانح بلا صلاحية المال) الذي يُوجَّه إلى صفحة بلا مال.
  • إعدادات Event Notifications: notification-settings.manage (الصلاحية القائمة لصفحة Notification Rules).
  • البريد يحمل روابط لا مرفقات.

Validation rules

إعدادات الأحداث: مفتاح من الكتالوج (Rule::in)، والأهمية Enum، والمستلمون أدوار موجودة.

Exceptional and edge cases

  • فشل البريد: الإشعار الداخلي يُرسل، وتُعاد المحاولة عبر الطابور (3 مرات)، وتُسجَّل في failed_jobs.
  • مستلم بلا بريد في HR: إشعار داخلي فقط.
  • تشغيل الأمر مرتين: ledger يمنع التكرار.
  • مسؤول MEAL للمحافظة غير معيّن: الاحتياط دور MEAL كاملًا.
  • حدث جماعي (توليد 12 شهرًا عند التفعيل): إشعار واحد مجمّع لا 12.

Data integrity

ledger + الإرسال بعد الالتزام (afterCommit) عبر الطابور.

Implementation notes

  • الالتزام بـ AlertDispatcher (RecipientFilter → AlertLedger::claim → notify)، وNotificationGrouper للتجميع.
  • كل مهمة تطلق أحداثها بنفسها (بند في Definition of Done). هذه المهمة تملك الكتالوج والمستلمين الأساسيين والتغطية والملخص، لا كتابة إشعارات كل وحدة من جديد.

Testing requirements

  • لكل حدث في الكتالوج: يصل للمستلمين المباشرين ولـ MEAL والإدارة، ولا يصل لغيرهم (Notification::fake).
  • لا تكرار للشخص المزدوج الدور، والمُحدِث لا يُشعَر.
  • أحداث المال بلا مبالغ لغير المالية.
  • الملخص الشهري: المحتوى لكل مستلم، والترجمة، وعدم التكرار، مع تجميد الوقت.
  • EventCatalogCoverageTest يفشل عند إضافة حدث بلا إشعار.

Acceptance criteria

  • فريق MEAL والإدارة العامة يرون كل حركة على المشروع والمقترح والتقرير، فورًا أو في الملخص اليومي بحسب الأهمية.
  • مدراء البرامج وMEAL وPR يتلقون ملخصًا شهريًا واحدًا.
  • الإدارة تعدّل مستلمي أي حدث من الإعدادات دون مطوّر.

Mistakes to avoid

  • إرسال البريد متزامنًا داخل الطلب، أو تضمين بيانات مالية.
  • إشعار لكل شهر مولّد بدل إشعار مجمّع.
  • كتابة مستلمين بأسماء أشخاص.

## Role and goal
You are implementing Task 22 of the HC Tracking proposal-lifecycle correction plan in this Laravel 13 / Livewire 4 / Flux UI 2 repository. The outcome: every uploaded document is written to disk encrypted (AES-256-GCM through `Illuminate\Encryption\Encrypter`, with a dedicated `FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` that is never `APP_KEY`) and decrypted only while the existing protected download and preview routes stream it; existing plaintext files are encrypted by a resumable command; the key can be rotated; one file can be extracted in an emergency. Today files sit in private storage behind policy-checked controllers, but anyone who reaches the server or its backups can read them. In the corrected story the concept note, the proposal file, the agreement, monthly-report evidence (Task 17), aggregated donor-report submissions (Task 19) and department-task deliveries such as media files (Task 31) are all uploads, and they inherit encryption through `App\Support\StoredFiles`. Authorization, URLs, upload rules and limits do not change.

## Scope
### In scope
- Migration `add_encryption_key_id_to_file_tables`: `encryption_key_id` varchar(20) nullable on `media`, `report_files`, `task_attachments` (and any file table already merged by another task).
- Config: an `encryption` block (propose `config/filesystems.php` or a new `config/files.php`): cipher `aes-256-gcm`, `key` (`FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), `key_id` (`FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID`, falling back to a constant such as `k1` when empty), `previous_keys` (`FILE_ENCRYPTION_PREVIOUS_KEYS`, `id:key,id:key`).
- A small keyring (propose `App\Support\FileKeyring`): validates keys, returns the current `[id, Encrypter]` and an `Encrypter` by key id.
- Update `App\Support\StoredFiles`: `save()` encrypts every new upload; add `putEncrypted()`, `contents()`, `stream()`; one routine that rewrites one stored file (used by both commands).
- Update the seven controllers to read through `StoredFiles::stream()` with the same guards, headers, filenames and route names.
- Models: `encryption_key_id` in `#[Fillable]` and `@property`; optional `isEncrypted()`.
- `FileType::mimeType()` (or one shared map) so responses set `Content-Type` from the validated type.
- `App\Exceptions\UnreadableStoredFile` (`php artisan make:exception`) rendering a friendly page built on `x-errors.page`; keys in `lang/{en,ar}/errors.php`.
- Commands: `files:encrypt-existing {--dry-run} {--chunk=100}`; `security:reencrypt --files`; `files:decrypt` (signature below).
- `.env.example`: `FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY=`, `FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID=`, `FILE_ENCRYPTION_PREVIOUS_KEYS=` with comments, all empty (the `SecretHygieneTest` regex also matches `*_KEY_ID`).
- Test bootstrap: a random key per Feature test (e.g. `beforeEach` in `tests/Pest.php`), never a committed key.
- Key backup/rotation text: no deployment guide exists yet (Task 29 writes the runbook). Propose where it goes; by default put it in your report for Tasks 27/29 and in `.env.example` comments; create no doc file without approval.
### Out of scope
Running the migration of existing files on staging/production (Task 27 rehearses, Task 29 runs it); upload rules, size, types, rate limits, routes, policies; new upload features (Tasks 07, 17, 19, 31); encrypting database columns (already `security:reencrypt` without `--files`).

## Business rules
- Every upload stored after deployment is encrypted, no exception. With no valid key the upload fails closed (friendly message on the file field, error logged); plaintext is never written as a fallback.
- `SecureUpload`, `max:5120`, `mimes` and `extensions` run on the original upload in the component's validation, before `StoredFiles` is called. Encryption happens only inside `StoredFiles`, after validation.
- `size` keeps the original byte count; the ciphertext (base64 JSON, about a third larger) never counts against the 5MB limit.
- `encryption_key_id` NULL = legacy plaintext, streamed as is until the command encrypts it.
- Download/preview URLs, route names, download filenames, IDOR guards, `isFundingPaper()` 403, `throttle:files` and headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, preview `Content-Type`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`, `Cache-Control: private`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` for images) stay identical.
- Encrypt raw bytes: `$encrypter->encrypt($bytes, false)` / `decrypt($payload, false)` (no serialization), 32-byte key, cipher `aes-256-gcm` (GCM tag = integrity check).

## Security and authorization
- `FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is independent from `APP_KEY`: rotating one never breaks the other. Never use the `Crypt` facade or the default encrypter for files.
- Never log, print, return or commit a key, plaintext or payload (not in tests, `phpunit.xml`, `.env.example` or exceptions). gitleaks runs in CI.
- Controllers keep `Gate::authorize('view', $parent)` and the ownership check first; decrypt only after both pass.
- `Content-Type` comes from the validated `FileType`, never from the stored bytes (ciphertext detects as text) or the client MIME.
- User-facing errors reveal no path and no crypto detail: «تعذّر فتح الملف، راجع قسم تقنية المعلومات» / "The file could not be opened. Please contact IT." `Log::error` carries table, row id and key id only.
- `files:decrypt` writes plaintext only to an explicit destination outside the upload folders and `public/`, refuses to overwrite, prints only the destination, and reminds the operator to delete it.
- Commands use `ConfirmableTrait` for real runs in production and print "run with --dry-run first".

## Validation
- No new user input. Each command exits with FAILURE, a clear message and no writes when: the key is missing; `Encrypter::supported($key, 'aes-256-gcm')` fails (accept the `base64:` prefix like `APP_KEY`); the key id is empty, longer than 20 characters or not `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; a previous-key entry is malformed or reuses the current id.
- Upload with a misconfigured key: error on the file field «تخزين الملفات غير مهيأ، راجع قسم تقنية المعلومات» / "File storage is not configured. Please contact IT." in all four forms; propose the mechanism (e.g. a typed exception the shared forms translate).

## Edge cases and concurrency
- Wrong key, corrupt file or unknown key id: decrypt BEFORE building the response, catch `DecryptException`, throw `UnreadableStoredFile` → friendly page, error logged; never a raw 500 or a half-sent stream. The Office preview sees a non-OK response and shows its existing error state (no JS change).
- Command interrupted mid-batch: rows with `encryption_key_id` are skipped on rerun; leftover temp files are unreferenced and `files:prune` removes them after its grace period.
- Row without a file on disk, reference-only `report_files`/`task_attachments` (`original_name` NULL), or `disk` other than `local`: skip, count, log.
- A user replaces or deletes the file while the command processes it: lock the row, re-check `path` and `encryption_key_id` after the lock; if changed, discard the temp file and skip.
- Two command runs at once: implement `Illuminate\Contracts\Console\Isolatable` on all three commands.
- Livewire keeps the plaintext temporary upload in `livewire-tmp` (it copies on store). Delete the temporary file after a successful encrypted save; abandoned ones stay until `files:prune` (24h) — state this residual risk in your report.
- Replacing a file: the new upload is encrypted; the old file (plaintext or encrypted) is forgotten after the save, as today.
- Backups taken before the run still hold plaintext: handoff note for Tasks 27/29.

## Data integrity
- Per-file sequence from the plan: read original → encrypt → write `{path}.enc.tmp` → read back, decrypt, `hash_equals(sha256(original), sha256(decrypted))` → atomic replace → set `encryption_key_id` in a transaction. Never overwrite the original before the verified copy exists.
- Known gap: between the rename and the row update a concurrent download serves ciphertext as plaintext. Propose in plan mode the variant: write a new sibling path `{dir}/{random}.{type}`, verify, then in one transaction (row locked, unchanged) set `path` and `encryption_key_id`, and delete the old plaintext after commit (leftovers are caught by `files:prune`). Pick one with the developer.
- The `local` disk has `'throw' => false`: `put()`/`move()`/`delete()` return false instead of throwing. Check every return value and abort that file.
- Commands update rows through the query builder (no `updated_at` change, no activity) under `Activity::withoutRecording`, one row per transaction with `lockForUpdate`, like `ReencryptSecrets`.
- Migration: additive nullable column, no backfill; `down()` refuses (throws) when any row has a non-null `encryption_key_id`, then drops the column.
- `files:encrypt-existing --dry-run` reports per table: to encrypt, already encrypted, missing on disk, skipped. After a real run "to encrypt" must be 0 (the acceptance query).

## Implementation guidance
- `declare(strict_types=1);` everywhere; `final` support classes; `php artisan make:migration add_encryption_key_id_to_file_tables --no-interaction`, `php artisan make:command EncryptExistingFiles --no-interaction`, `php artisan make:command DecryptStoredFile --no-interaction`.
- New upload path: `{directory}/{Str::random(40)}.{type->value}` (extension from `FileType`, per `.ai/rules/enums.md`), contents from `$upload->get()`.
- Build responses with `response()->streamDownload(fn () => print($bytes), $name, $headers, $disposition)` after decryption; keep each controller's header set; downloads keep `assertDownload()` behaviour.
- Keyring: parse keys like `EncryptionServiceProvider` (`base64:` prefix), build one `Encrypter` per key id, memoize per request.
- `security:reencrypt` without `--files` behaves exactly as today (`ReencryptSecretsCommandTest` stays green); with `--files` re-keys every file whose `encryption_key_id` is not the current id, supports `--dry-run`. Confirm in plan mode whether `--files` also runs the database columns.
- `files:decrypt {--id=}` is ambiguous (ids repeat across the three tables): propose `files:decrypt {table : media|report_files|task_attachments} {--id=} {--to=}`.
- Console output in English (like existing commands), counts and ids only.
```php
final class StoredFiles
{
    /** Encrypt and write the bytes; returns the key id to store on the row. */
    public static function putEncrypted(string $disk, string $path, string $contents): string {}

    /** Plaintext bytes: decrypted when $keyId is set, raw for legacy rows. @throws UnreadableStoredFile */
    public static function contents(string $disk, string $path, ?string $keyId): string {}

    /** The caller has already authorized. Decrypts first, then builds the response. */
    public static function stream(string $disk, string $path, ?string $keyId, string $downloadName, FileType $type, array $headers = [], string $disposition = 'attachment'): StreamedResponse {}
}
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New uploads in the project, proposal, report and task forms are ciphertext on disk with `encryption_key_id`; download and preview return the original bytes.
- [ ] Legacy rows download until encrypted; after `files:encrypt-existing` the dry run reports 0 plaintext files and a rerun is a no-op.
- [ ] `security:reencrypt --files` rotates the key and downloads still work after the old key is removed.
- [ ] Wrong or missing key gives a localized message and a log line, never a raw 500, a path or crypto details.
- [ ] `MediaTest`, `ProjectFileCrudTest`, `PrivateStorageRoutesTest`, `SecretHygieneTest` pass; Pint clean.
- [ ] Merged by end of day 5 so Tasks 31 and 17 inherit encryption.

## Do not
- Use `APP_KEY` or the `Crypt` facade for files, or add a dependency (the Encrypter is built in).
- Run `SecureUpload`, type or size checks after encryption or on ciphertext.
- Overwrite the original before the encrypted copy is verified, or ignore a `false` from `Storage`.
- Change routes, policies, rate limits, add public or signed URLs, or serve the detected MIME.
- Fall back to plaintext when the key is missing; log or print a key or plaintext; commit a key anywhere.

## Working method
- Start in plan mode: restate the task in 5 bullets, list files you will touch, list open questions (D-19, config location, key id default, same-path vs new-path rewrite, `--files` semantics, `files:decrypt` signature, where the key-backup text goes); wait for approval.
- Implement in small steps; after each step run the narrowest relevant tests.
- Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` after PHP changes.
- If you discover a durable rule or trap, record it with the Boost `record-rule` tool (not native memory).
- Do not commit, push, or run destructive commands (`migrate:fresh`, seeders that reset roles, deleting storage) unless the developer asks.
- Never run anything against production.
- Stay inside Task 22's scope; note anything else as a follow-up.

## Report back
Your final message must contain: summary; files changed; migration added; tests run with pass/fail output; decisions assumed (D-19, config location, key id default, rewrite variant, `--files` semantics, `files:decrypt` signature, temp-upload deletion); follow-ups (residual plaintext in `livewire-tmp` and old backups). Handoff facts: Tasks 07, 17, 19 and 31 must store through `StoredFiles::save()`/`putEncrypted()`, stream through `StoredFiles::stream()`, add `encryption_key_id` to any new file table and register it in the commands' table list; Task 27 (Dev 1, rehearsal on the production copy) needs the dry-run counts on local data, the time per 100 files and the backup-before-run step; Task 29 needs the env variables, the exact command sequence (`--dry-run`, real run, verification count), the rotation steps and where the key copy is kept, plus the fallback if the existing-file migration is deferred after launch (R9).

Objective

تطبيق «لازم ننتبه ع الرفع حصرًا كلو مشفّر». الملفات اليوم في تخزين خاص ومحمية بالمسارات، لكنها غير مشفّرة على القرص: من يصل إلى الخادم أو إلى النسخ الاحتياطية يقرؤها. المطلوب تشفير كل ملف عند الكتابة وفك تشفيره عند التنزيل أو المعاينة فقط.

Implementation scope

  • تغليف App\Support\StoredFiles: put يشفّر المحتوى بمفتاح مستقل FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (AES-256-GCM عبر Illuminate\Encryption\Encrypter)، وstream يفك التشفير.
  • أعمدة encryption_key_id (varchar 20، nullable) في media وreport_files وtask_attachments وكل جدول ملفات جديد. NULL يعني ملفًا قديمًا غير مشفّر.
  • مسارات التنزيل والمعاينة القائمة تقرأ عبر StoredFiles::stream، فلا تتغير الروابط.
  • أمر files:encrypt-existing {--dry-run} {--chunk=100}: يشفّر القائم على دفعات، idempotent وقابل للاستئناف.
  • توسيع security:reencrypt لتدوير مفتاح الملفات (--files).
  • أمر طوارئ files:decrypt {--id=} لاستخراج ملف بعينه.

Required deliverables

ترحيل الأعمدة، StoredFiles المحدّث، الأوامر الثلاثة، .env.example (FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY، FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID)، توثيق النسخ الاحتياطي للمفتاح في دليل النشر، اختبارات.

Business rules

  • كل رفع جديد بعد النشر مشفّر بلا استثناء.
  • فحص الأمان (SecureUpload) والتحقق من النوع والحجم يجريان قبل التشفير على المحتوى الأصلي.
  • الحد 5MB للأصل. الحجم المشفّر أكبر بنحو الثلث ولا يُحتسب على المستخدم.
  • الملف القديم يبقى قابلًا للقراءة إلى أن يُشفَّر بالأمر.

Security and permissions

  • المفتاح ليس APP_KEY، فتدوير أحدهما لا يكسر الآخر. لا يُرفع إلى المستودع (gitleaks يفحص)، ويُحفظ نسخة خارج الخادم.
  • لا تغيير في التفويض: التنزيل ما زال يمر بالسياسة وفحص انتماء الملف لسجله وحد المعدل.
  • رسائل الخطأ لا تكشف المسار ولا تفاصيل التشفير.
  • --dry-run إلزامي في الإنتاج قبل التشغيل الفعلي.

Validation rules

لا إدخال مستخدم جديد. الأمر يرفض التشغيل إن لم يكن المفتاح مضبوطًا، أو كان طوله غير صالح.

Exceptional and edge cases

  • ملف تالف أو مفتاح خاطئ: DecryptException تُلتقط، ويُعرض «تعذّر فتح الملف، راجع قسم تقنية المعلومات»، ويُسجَّل خطأ بمعرّف الملف.
  • انقطاع الأمر في منتصف دفعة: كل ملف يُكتب إلى مسار مؤقت، ثم يُستبدل الأصل ذريًا، ثم يُحدَّث الصف. إعادة التشغيل تتخطى ما له encryption_key_id.
  • ملف موجود في الصف ومفقود من القرص (سجلات «مرجع فقط»): يُتخطى ويُسجَّل.
  • المعاينة (docx-preview، xlsx) تستقبل المحتوى المفكوك عبر المسار المحمي، فلا تأثر.
  • files:prune (اليتامى) يعمل على المسارات كما هو.

Data integrity

  • ترتيب آمن لكل ملف: قراءة الأصل ← تشفير ← كتابة path.enc.tmp ← إعادة القراءة وفك التشفير والتحقق من التطابق (hash) ← استبدال ذري ← تحديث encryption_key_id في معاملة.
  • نسخة احتياطية كاملة للتخزين قبل التشغيل في الإنتاج (Task 27).

Implementation notes

final class StoredFiles
{
    public static function putEncrypted(string $disk, string $path, string $contents): string /* key id */ {}
    public static function stream(string $disk, string $path, ?string $keyId, string $downloadName, string $mime): StreamedResponse {}
}
  • الملفات ≤ 5MB، فالتشفير في الذاكرة مقبول، ولا حاجة لتشفير متدفق.

Testing requirements

  • البايتات المخزنة ≠ الأصل، والتنزيل يعيد الأصل بالضبط (مقارنة hash).
  • ملف قديم بلا مفتاح يُنزَّل كما هو.
  • مفتاح خاطئ: رسالة ودية وخطأ مسجل، لا 500 خام.
  • الأمر idempotent ويتخطى المشفّر، و--dry-run لا يكتب شيئًا.
  • التنزيل بلا صلاحية ما زال 403 (PrivateStorageRoutesTest).
  • تدوير المفتاح يعيد التشفير ويبقي التنزيل سليمًا.

Acceptance criteria

  • بعد النشر والأمر: 0 صفوف ملفات لها ملف على القرص بلا encryption_key_id (استعلام فحص).
  • MediaTest وProjectFileCrudTest وPrivateStorageRoutesTest تمر.

Mistakes to avoid

  • استعمال APP_KEY لتشفير الملفات.
  • فحص الأمان بعد التشفير.
  • كتابة فوق الأصل قبل التحقق من النسخة المشفرة.

Output and handoff to the next task

تخزين مشفّر يستعمله كل رفع في المهام 07 و17 و19 و31. ترحيل الملفات القائمة يجري في Task 27/29.

## Role and goal
You are implementing Task 23 of the HC Tracking proposal-lifecycle correction plan in this Laravel 13 / Livewire 4 / Flux UI 2 repository. The outcome: a supervision map whose default source is HR (the direct manager of the employee's current position, `positions.direct_manager_id`, read through Task 30's `EmployeeProfile`), plus a local `supervisions` table (supervisor HR employee → supervisee HR employee) for exceptions and additions only, maintained in a **Supervision** tab of **Users & Roles** (`/admin/users`) that also shows the HR relations read-only; and three uses of it: (1) overdue-item escalation also reaches the supervisor, next to the program manager; (2) a **My Team** card on **Home** (`/home`) shows each supervisor what their people have outstanding; (3) a read helper that Task 17 uses to let a supervisor prepare a monthly report on behalf of a supervisee. In the corrected story center managers own projects and send monthly reports, and "every manager must check" their team; supervision is a routing fact, never an extra permission.

## Business rules
- Nobody supervises themselves; a pair is unique, including against HR (a local row duplicating the HR direct manager is refused: «هذه المتابعة موجودة في HR»); a direct loop (A supervises B while B supervises A) is refused; longer chains are allowed; a person may have several supervisors.
- Both employees are active in HR when the row is created. An employee who later becomes inactive keeps the row (shown "inactive") but has no effect in the helper, the card or escalation.
- Escalation: at the program-manager stage (`escalate_manager_after_days` within `escalation_catch_up_days`, both from `NotificationSettings`), the active supervisors of the people named on the item (`DeadlineItem::directUserIds` mapped to employee ids) also receive a Critical alert, key `notifications.alerts.escalation.supervisor`, stage `supervisor:{due}`. Skip anyone already notified as program manager for that item and the named person themselves. Items without named people (watched by roles) get no supervisor escalation. Propose in plan mode whether a task's creator (also in `directUserIds`) should count as "named".
- **My Team** card: shown only to a user with a linked employee who supervises at least one active employee. Sections: overdue open tasks assigned to supervisees (count per person + link); unsent monthly reports (only if Task 17 is merged); donor reports due for supervisees (only if Task 19 is merged, and only for holders of `funding-agreements.view`, no amounts). Unbuilt sections are follow-ups, never placeholder tables.
- Removing a supervision takes effect immediately in the helper, card and escalation.

## Security and authorization
- `supervisions.manage`: `Gate::authorize` inside each Action and at the top of each Livewire method; the tab is hidden and its methods return 403 without it. The route keeps `viewAny` (`access-management.manage-users`); General Manager holds both. Do not widen the route without approval; report the gap if a role gets `supervisions.manage` alone.
- Supervision grants no visibility: `TaskVisibilityScope` is untouched. The card's task query runs as the signed-in user so the global scope applies. For task escalations, keep only supervisors for whom `TaskVisibilityScope::allows($user, $task)` (or `TaskPolicy::view`) is true, so a title never reaches someone who cannot open it; other modules go through `RecipientFilter` via `AlertDispatcher::send()`.
- Employee ids are re-checked server-side against HR (exists, active); the client picker list is never trusted. `created_by` = `auth()->id()`. Ids held by the component are `#[Locked]`.
- Audit: create and delete record activities with both names.

## Validation
Messages in `lang/ar/users.php` and `lang/en/users.php`:
- `supervisorEmployeeId`, `superviseeEmployeeId`: required, integer, an active HR employee — «اختر موظفًا فعّالًا» / "Choose an active employee". Use a closure querying `HrEmployee` (or `Rule::exists(HrEmployee::class, 'id')->where('is_active', true)` after proving it uses the `hr` connection).
- different: «لا يمكن أن يتابع الشخص نفسه» / "A person cannot supervise themselves".
- unique pair: «هذه المتابعة مسجّلة مسبقًا» / "This supervision already exists".
- reverse pair: «لا يمكن أن يتابع شخصان بعضهما» / "Two people cannot supervise each other".
- already in HR: «هذه المتابعة موجودة في HR» / "This supervision already comes from HR".
- Import (if built): header row required, row cap (propose 500), every row valid; errors listed with line numbers «السطر :line: :error» / "Line :line: :error"; the whole batch is rejected on any error.

## Edge cases and concurrency
- Double submit: the unique index rejects the second insert; catch `UniqueConstraintViolationException` and show the duplicate message, never a 500.
- Two admins adding A→B and B→A at once: an application check alone cannot stop it. Propose stored generated columns `pair_low`/`pair_high` (`LEAST`/`GREATEST`) with a unique index (blocks duplicates and direct loops in the database), or a lock on the ordered pair; pick one in plan mode.
- Removing a row already removed: no-op with a message. Permission revoked mid-session: 403.
- Employee without a tracking user: no notification; tasks still counted by employee id on the card.
- Import with a bad row: nothing written. Pairs already present: unchanged and counted, not errors (confirm).
- Scanner cost: load the whole map and HR active flags once per scan; map user ids ↔ employee ids in one query; no per-item queries.

## Data integrity
- Unique index on the pair (plus the loop guard you choose); FK only on `created_by`; no FK to HR.
- Add, remove and import each run in one `DB::transaction` through Eloquent so `RecordsActivity` fires; import is all-or-nothing (propose one activity per row or a single summary event).
- `utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / InnoDB DYNAMIC (`DatabaseEncodingTest`); working `down()`.
- Optional seed in a demo seeder under `Activity::withoutRecording` with active HR employees only; add the model to `tests/Feature/DatabaseSeederTest.php` if seeded.

## Implementation guidance
- `php artisan make:migration create_supervisions_table --no-interaction`, `php artisan make:model Supervision --factory --no-interaction`, `php artisan make:class Support/SupervisionMap --no-interaction` (adjust namespace, `declare(strict_types=1);`).
- Flux modals bound with `wire:model`, never `:open`; `x-ui.*` components; logical classes (`ms-*`, `pe-*`, `text-start`); "inactive" uses a status token plus an icon, not colour alone; full `@php … @endphp` blocks only.
- Card: one `myTeam()` computed on the dashboard with a fixed number of queries (supervisee ids, HR names, tasks grouped by assignee, one per optional section); when the user supervises nobody, only the first query runs.
- Escalation sketch inside the manager-stage branch:
```php
$supervisorUserIds = $this->supervisorUsersFor($item, exclude: [...$managers, ...$item->directUserIds]);
if ($supervisorUserIds !== []) {
    $payload = $this->dispatcher->payload($item->module, NotificationPriority::Critical, 'notifications.alerts.escalation.supervisor', $params, $item->subjectType, $item->subjectId);
    $sent += $this->dispatcher->send('escalation', "supervisor:{$due}", $payload, $supervisorUserIds);
}
```

## Acceptance criteria

## Do not
- Give supervisors implicit permissions or bypass `TaskVisibilityScope`.
- Add a foreign key to an HR table, write to HR, or `whereHas()` across the `hr` connection.
- Hard-code escalation days; add a notification module without its icon/banners; put module logic in `RecipientResolver`.
- Accept a partial import, or trust the client picker list.
- Bind a Flux modal with `:open`, or use the `@php(...)` shorthand.

## Working method
- Start in plan mode: restate the task in 5 bullets, list files you will touch, list open questions (D-13, activity module, loop guard, import form, task creator in escalation, card sections available now); wait for approval.
- Implement in small steps; after each step run the narrowest relevant tests.
- Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` after PHP changes.
- If you discover a durable rule or trap, record it with the Boost `record-rule` tool (not native memory).
- Do not commit, push, or run destructive commands (`migrate:fresh`, seeders that reset roles, deleting storage) unless the developer asks.
- Never run anything against production.
- Stay inside Task 23's scope; note anything else as a follow-up.

## Report back
Your final message must contain: summary; files changed; migration added; tests run with pass/fail output; decisions assumed (D-13 HR source and how local exceptions combine, activity module, loop guard, import approach, escalation "named people"); whether the R9 cut (My Team card) was applied; follow-ups (card sections waiting for Tasks 17/19). Handoff facts: for Task 17 and Task 21 the exact `SupervisionMap` signatures, that they merge HR direct managers with local exceptions and return active HR employee ids, and that supervision adds no permission (the monthly-report policy must still require `reports.create/update`); for Task 19/21 how to add the donor-report and digest sections; for Task 26 the new lang keys, the tab and card names and any `data-tour` anchors; for Task 28 a UAT scenario (link, escalate, card).

## Business rules
- No literal UI text in Blade or rendered PHP: `__('group.key')` / `trans_choice()` with the key in both languages. Shared words in `common.php`, titles in `titles.php` (`#[Title('titles.x')]`), dates via `->translatedFormat(__('formats.date'))`; `lang/ar.json` holds only vendor sentence keys; never name a group file `results`, `of`, `to`, `files` or `showing`.
- Unified Arabic terms: المذكرة المفاهيمية، المقترح، الاتفاقية، الأثر (Impact)، النتيجة (Outcome)، المُخرَج (Output)، النشاط (Activity)، المستهدف، التحقق. Grep `lang/ar` for synonyms the task introduced and align them.
- Stored values stay English; only labels translate (`$case->label()`).
- Arabic plurals use explicit ranges `{0}|{1}|{2}|[3,10]|[11,*]`; every `:placeholder` of the English text survives.
- Indicator names show in the user's language from **Indicator Library**, the other language as a secondary line.
- Codes (`R8.A1.I1`), numbers, amounts and project numbers render LTR-isolated (`x-ui.project-number` for project numbers, `<bdi dir="ltr">` otherwise); mixed Arabic/English cells use `dir="auto"`.
- Tours: required for **Indicator Library**, **Logical Framework** tab in **Proposal**, **Reviewers** panel, **Monthly Report**, **Monthly Matrix**, **Plan** tab in **Proposal**, **Department Tasks**, **Donor Report Builder**, **My Reporting Duties**; every other new page route gets at least an `intro`. Tour copy explains what the user sees and does; it never contains data.

## Security and authorization
- No sensitive data in text: no amounts in notifications, emails, tour copy or empty states meant for users without money permissions; never add an `:amount` placeholder the task did not pass.
- Error and validation messages are non-technical: no table, column, class, path, SQL or encryption details.
- Tour steps point only at elements the page already renders for that user; never render a hidden money element so a step can reach it. Data hooks carry no record ids.

## Validation
- Every validation message of Task `<TASK_NUMBER>` (component `validate()` message arrays and Action `ValidationException::withMessages()`) resolves to a key present in `lang/ar/<module>.php` and `lang/en/<module>.php`; none falls back to Laravel's generic English sentence in the Arabic UI. Follow the per-field message style of `ManagesAgreementForm::saveAgreement()`.

## Edge cases and concurrency
- Long Arabic labels in grids, badges and buttons: wrap or truncate with a `title`, never clip meaning.
- Codes and numbers inside Arabic sentences: isolate the placeholder value at render time.
- **Monthly Matrix** month columns and grid keyboard navigation (Tasks 13, 17, 18) must follow the reading direction (in RTL, ArrowRight moves toward the start). Fix only if local and trivial; otherwise log a follow-up for the owning task.
- Tab-scoped tour steps only appear when that tab is open; the intro must still read well when it is not.
- Parallel runs editing the same lang files: keep edits grouped per module; on conflicts keep both keys and rerun `LocalizationTest`.
- `user-guide`: decisions marked "افتراضي مطبّق" are described as current behaviour; Tasks 24/25 are out of the October window and are not described; features cut under R9 are not described as shipped.

## Role and goal
You are preparing Task 27 of the HC Tracking proposal-lifecycle correction plan: the data-migration rehearsal on a copy of production, and the rollback plan. You are a preparer, not an operator. You write read-only check SQL, the rehearsal procedure, the runbook and the rollback plan, and you fill the rehearsal report from outputs a human pastes to you. You never connect to production or to the rehearsal copy, and you never execute anything there; an authorised person runs every step. This matters because the release rewrites the core of the corrected story on live data (project = HR center, one donor and at most one agreement per proposal, draft projects without dates, the proposal state machine, Indicator Library, the four-level logframe, proposal milestones and department tasks, auto-generated monthly reports, aggregated donor reports, auto-generated transfer records, encrypted files). Task 29 deploys from your runbook, so it needs measured durations, verified before/after counts, and a rollback that was actually tried at least once.

## Scope
### In scope (documents under `docs/superpowers/specs/`; confirm the names in plan mode)

  - Part A: the rehearsal procedure.
  - Part B: the production sequence, as a draft that Task 29 finalises.
  - Part C: the rollback plan.
  - The migration and command inventory: run order, owning task, pre-check guard inside `up()`, backfill, lossy or failing `down()`, and size risk.
- Create `2026-10-27-proposal-lifecycle-rehearsal-report.md`. It is a template that you fill from the operator's pasted outputs: timings per step, counts before/after, errors, the idempotency re-runs, the rollback test, the copy-deletion confirmation, and sign-off.
- If Task 22 already documented the backup of `FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (search `docs/` for it), link to that instead of repeating it.
### Out of scope
- Executing anything on production or on the copy. Humans do that; Task 29 deploys.
- Fixing a migration, command or seeder. That goes to the owning task in a new session, and then the whole rehearsal is repeated.
- Writing UPDATE/DELETE/DDL for any shared database. A data correction that management decides on becomes a reviewed migration or command in Task 03 or Task 05.
- The deployment checklist, production smoke tests and 48-hour monitoring (Task 29), and UAT (Task 28). Editing the plan.

## Business rules
- Any non-zero blocking pre-check stops the release until management decides. The blocking checks, from the plan:
  - proposals with more than one agreement;
  - proposals with no agreement;
  - projects in `submitted` / `approved`;
  - `draft` projects carrying `start_date` or `end_date`;
  - centers with more than one open project (D-30), unless management records a decision.
- `hr:map-project-centers --apply` runs only after management has reviewed the dry-run matching (ambiguous and unmatched projects listed).
- Every command that has `--dry-run` runs dry first and then for real. Both outputs go into the report.
- Take a full backup (database + storage) before each step, and check integrity after it.
- Record the start and end time of each step. These times size the maintenance window.
- The rehearsal passes only if it runs end to end without manual intervention. A manual fix means it failed: the fix goes to the owning task, then the rehearsal runs again from a fresh copy.
- The rollback is tried at least once. The copy is deleted after the rehearsal, and the operator confirms this in the report.
- On the copy, as on production: no `RolesAndPermissionsSeeder`, no `db:seed`, no `migrate:fresh`, no `migrate:refresh`.

## Security and authorization
- The SQL is `SELECT` only (including `information_schema`): no DDL, no DML, no `INTO OUTFILE`, no procedures. Recommend a read-only DB user.
- Results record counts and record ids only. No names, emails, amounts, account numbers or file names.
- The environment is closed, and production keys never reach developer machines.
  - The rehearsal `FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is a throwaway key generated on the rehearsal host. It is never the production key, and it is destroyed with the copy.
  - The copy holds APP_KEY-encrypted columns: `users.two_factor_secret` and `two_factor_recovery_codes`; `accounts.account_number`, `iban`, `swift_code` and `authorized_person`. The operator chooses between two options and records the choice: keep the production APP_KEY on the closed host only, or rehearse without it and list which pages and logins cannot be checked. Never run `key:generate` on the copy.
- The rehearsal `.env` neutralises every outbound effect, so the copy never emails, notifies or pushes to real staff:
  - `MAIL_MAILER=log` and `BROADCAST_CONNECTION=log`;
  - no queue worker and no scheduler cron (the `jobs` rows copied from production must never run);
  - `HR_DB_*` pointing at an HR snapshot or a read-only replica (needed by `hr:map-project-centers` and `EmployeeProfile`; never writable);
  - `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=false`.
- Migrations need ALTER, INDEX, REFERENCES and CREATE on the schema. Ask the operator to confirm the production DB user has them. If it does not, the runbook uses a separate migration account that the operator supplies. Never write credentials into any document.

## Validation
No user input. Validate the deliverables:
- Every SQL check has an id, a purpose, an owning task, a blocking/informational flag and an expected result, and it runs on both MariaDB and MySQL.
- Every runbook step has the command (with `<placeholders>`), the expected output, the measured duration, the backup point and the action to take on failure.
- Every command in the runbook exists in `php artisan list`, with the flags shown.

## Edge cases and concurrency
- **A migration fails midway.** MySQL/MariaDB do not roll back DDL, so the migration may be half applied. Stop, record the migration and the failing statement, and restore from the backup. Never hand-patch the schema.
- **Data guards stop a migration.** Task 03's migrations throw before any DDL and print offender ids. That is the expected outcome on dirty data: record it and stop.
- **Rollback proof.** Prove each `down()` on the copy with `migrate:rollback --step=<n>` back to the baseline, then migrate forward again. Flag lossy reversals: Task 05's status conversion, backfilled columns, and `transfers_tracking`. On production, rollback means restoring the backup. Evaluate `migrate --force --step` so that each migration is its own batch.
- **`files:encrypt-existing` is interrupted.** A re-run skips rows that have `encryption_key_id`. Check that no `*.enc.tmp` file is left behind. Report the counts of skipped rows: reference-only `report_files` / `task_attachments` rows (`original_name IS NULL`) and rows whose file is missing on disk.
- **Disk space.** Encrypted files are about a third larger, and temp copies need room as well. Free space must be at least 1.5× the size of `storage/app/private`.
- **Encryption takes longer than the window.** Document the alternative: run it after `up`, because legacy files stay readable while `encryption_key_id IS NULL`. Mind the daily `files:prune` at 03:00. Record the decision of Dev 1 and management.
- **Idempotency.** Run every fill command a second time. The second run must report zero changes.
- **`permissions:sync` only adds.** Diff the role→permission snapshot: no existing pair may be removed, and the new pairs must match the signed matrix (Task 02).
- **The fill commands create no `activities` or `notifications` rows** (database-seeders rule). Compare the counts.
- **HR unreachable.** Migrations are unaffected; record it.
- **`migrate --pretend`.** Use it only to review the DDL. It does not prove that backfills are correct.

## Data integrity
- **Backups:**
  - a DB dump (`mysqldump`/`mariadb-dump --single-transaction --routines --triggers`);
  - an archive of `storage/app/private`;
  - `.env` kept separately in secure storage.
  A backup counts only after it has been restored once into a scratch schema and its counts match.
- **PRE checks, blocking.** Use these four exactly: `SELECT proposal_id, COUNT(*) FROM donor_proposal GROUP BY proposal_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;`, proposals with no `donor_proposal` row, projects with `status IN ('submitted','approved')`, and `draft` projects with dates.
- **PRE checks, informational** (each needs a management note):
  - active projects without a donor-approved proposal (`approved`, `active`, `final reports`, `completed`; this is Task 08's acceptance query);
  - proposals with no row in `project_proposal`;
  - donor-approved proposals missing `actual_date_begin` / `actual_date_end`;
  - `internal_project_number LIKE 'TEMP-%'`;
  - status distributions of `proposals` and `projects`;
  - indicator names that exist with more than one `measure` (the expected conflict count for Task 11's command);
  - file rows per table: total, stored, and `SUM(size)`. For `media`, every row is stored; for `report_files` / `task_attachments`, stored means `original_name IS NOT NULL`;
  - the role→permission snapshot, and users per role (counts only);
  - row counts of every touched table, `activities`, `notifications`, `jobs` and `failed_jobs`;
  - `annual_plans` (expected 8; unchanged, Task 24 is out of the window);
  - projects without `center_id`, centers with more than one open project, project cities without any HR center (R10, D-30);
  - active projects at deploy and the number of months `monthly-reports:backfill --from=2026-10` should create.
- **POST checks:**
  - `proposals.donor_id IS NULL` = 0;
  - agreements whose `donor_id` differs from their proposal's = 0;
  - the unique index on `donor_proposal.proposal_id` and the composite FK are present by name in `information_schema` (names from Task 03's handoff);
  - no `submitted` / `approved` projects, and no `draft` project with dates;
  - every new table and column exists with utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
  - every new permission exists, and no PRE pair is missing;
  - `indicators.library_indicator_id IS NULL` equals the conflict count the command reported;
  - stored file rows with `encryption_key_id IS NULL` = 0, apart from the rows the command reported as missing;
  - counts of tables the release must not change equal their PRE values;
  - `activities`, `notifications`, `jobs` and `failed_jobs` are unchanged by the fill commands (record separately the grouped `monthly_reports.generated` jobs, if the backfill emits them);
  - projects without `center_id` equal the list management accepted; no center has two open projects;
  - every project `active` at deploy has exactly one `monthly_reports` row per month from 2026-10 to its end month (none earlier, no duplicates).

  Build the expected tables and columns from the actual migrations, cross-checked against the plan.
- Shape for the existence checks:
  ```sql
  -- PRE-05 (informational, Task 08): active projects without a donor-approved proposal
  SELECT p.id FROM projects p
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM project_proposal pp JOIN proposals pr ON pr.id = pp.proposal_id
    WHERE pp.project_id = p.id AND pr.status IN ('approved','active','final reports','completed'));
  ```

## Implementation guidance
- Write the documents in Arabic, like the plan. Keep every command, SQL statement, table, column, status, permission and UI name in English. Use placeholders (`<db>`, `<app-path>`, `<backup-dir>`); never real hosts, users or paths.
- Part A steps:
  1. Restore the copy.
  2. Set up the safe `.env`.
  3. Run the PRE checks.
  4. Back up.
  5. `php artisan optimize:clear`.
  6. `migrate:status`.
  7. `migrate --pretend` (review).
  8. `migrate --force`.
  9. `migrate:status`.
  10. `permissions:sync --dry-run`, then `permissions:sync`.
  11. `hr:map-project-centers --dry-run`; management reviews the matching; then `--apply`.
  12. `meal:seed-indicator-library --dry-run`, then for real.
  13. `monthly-reports:backfill --from=2026-10 --dry-run`, then for real.
  14. `files:encrypt-existing --dry-run`, then for real.
  15. Re-run each command to prove idempotency.
  16. Run the POST checks.
  17. Open the main pages and download a sample of files of every type.
  18. Run the rollback test.
  19. Run forward again.
  20. Delete the copy.
- Part B follows Task 29's order, adapted to the rules:
  1. `php artisan down --render="errors::503" --retry=60`.
  2. Take the final backup (after `down`, so no write is lost).
  3. Pull the code.
  4. `composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader`.
  5. `npm run build`.
  6. `php artisan optimize:clear`.
  7. `migrate --force`.
  8. The dry-run/real pairs, in the Part A order (`permissions:sync`, `hr:map-project-centers` with the approved matching, `meal:seed-indicator-library`, `monthly-reports:backfill --from=2026-10`, `files:encrypt-existing` or its documented deferral).
  9. The POST checks.
  10. `optimize`.
  11. `queue:restart` and `reverb:restart` (or Supervisor).
  12. `up`.
  Put the rehearsal duration next to each step.
- Part C covers:
  - the triggers (a migration failure, systematic decryption errors, a broken approval path);
  - the decision owner;
  - the steps: `down` → restore the DB and storage TOGETHER (rows carry `encryption_key_id`, and old code would serve ciphertext) → the previous release → composer/npm → `optimize` → restart → `up`;
  - verification;
  - the data-loss window, and a user message in Arabic and English.

## Tests (Pest)
- Write no application tests.
- With the developer's agreement, run locally only:
  - `php artisan migrate:status`;
  - `php artisan migrate --pretend`;
  - the `--dry-run` commands (`permissions:sync`, `hr:map-project-centers`, `meal:seed-indicator-library`, `monthly-reports:backfill --from=2026-10`, `files:encrypt-existing`);
  - the command tests: Task 11's, Task 17's, Task 22's and Task 30's files (`grep -rl "meal:seed-indicator-library\|files:encrypt-existing\|monthly-reports:backfill\|hr:map-project-centers" tests`), plus `tests/Feature/SyncPermissionsCommandTest.php`, `tests/Feature/ReencryptSecretsCommandTest.php`, `tests/Feature/PruneStoredFilesTest.php` and `tests/Feature/DatabaseEncodingTest.php`, via `php artisan test --compact <file>`.
- Run every SQL check on the LOCAL database with Boost `database-query`, and label the results "local".
- The developer runs the full suite (`php artisan test --compact`) on the release commit. `phpunit.xml` targets `hc_tracking_test` with `RefreshDatabase`, so never point the suite at the copy: it would wipe it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The SQL file is `SELECT`-only, covers every check listed above, and every check ran locally with the results labelled.
- [ ] The runbook covers Parts A, B and C and the inventory, including `hr:map-project-centers` (after management review) and `monthly-reports:backfill --from=2026-10`; every command exists with the flags shown.
- [ ] The final rehearsal ran on the morning of day 13, before CP6.
- [ ] The report template has rows for each step's time, the counts before and after, the idempotency re-runs, the rollback test and the deletion of the copy.
- [ ] Once the operator's outputs are in, the report shows: the rehearsal passed without manual steps, the total duration is known, the rollback was tried once, and every blocking PRE check is 0 or has a management decision.

## Do not
- Run, or ask for access to run, anything on production or the copy.
- Skip `--dry-run`, run `RolesAndPermissionsSeeder` / `db:seed`, or use `migrate --graceful`.
- Write DML or DDL for shared databases.
- Put keys, credentials, personal data or amounts in any file or message.
- Treat a manual intervention as "passed".

## Working method
- Start in plan mode: restate the task in 5 bullets, list the files you will touch, list open questions; wait for approval.
- Implement in small steps; after each step run the narrowest relevant tests.
- Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` after PHP changes. This task changes no PHP.
- If you discover a durable rule or trap, record it with the Boost `record-rule` tool (not native memory).
- Do not commit, push, or run destructive commands (`migrate:fresh`, seeders that reset roles, deleting storage) unless the developer asks.
- Never run anything against production.
- Stay inside this task's scope; note anything else as a follow-up.

Objective

Implementation scope

  • استعادة نسخة الإنتاج (قاعدة + تخزين) على بيئة معزولة.
  • فحوص قبلية (استعلامات قراءة فقط): مقترحات بأكثر من اتفاقية، مقترحات بلا اتفاقية، مشاريع submitted/approved، مشاريع مسودة بتواريخ.
  • فحوص قبلية إضافية: مشاريع بلا مركز HR، ومراكز لها أكثر من مشروع مفتوح، ومراكز غير موجودة في HR للمدن 7 و8 و12 و13 و14 و17.
  • التشغيل: migrate ← permissions:sync --dry-run ثم الفعلي ← hr:map-project-centers --dry-run ثم --apply (بعد مراجعة الإدارة للمطابقة) ← meal:seed-indicator-library --dry-run ثم الفعلي ← monthly-reports:backfill --from=2026-10 --dry-run ثم الفعلي ← files:encrypt-existing --dry-run ثم الفعلي.
  • فحوص بعدية: الأعداد قبل/بعد، وعينات تنزيل ملفات، وصفحات رئيسية تعمل.
  • كتابة دليل التشغيل (runbook) وخطة التراجع.

Required deliverables

تقرير البروفة (الأزمنة، الأعداد، الأخطاء)، runbook، خطة تراجع.

Business rules

أي فحص قبلي غير صفري يوقف النشر حتى يُحسم مع الإدارة.

Security and permissions

النسخة على بيئة مغلقة، والمفاتيح الإنتاجية لا تُنسخ إلى أجهزة المطورين. تُحذف النسخة بعد البروفة.

Validation rules

لا ينطبق.

Exceptional and edge cases

فشل ترحيل في منتصفه: down() مجرَّب لكل ترحيل في البروفة. فشل التشفير: الملفات الأصلية باقية حتى الاستبدال الذري.

Data integrity

نسخة احتياطية كاملة قبل كل خطوة، وفحص سلامة بعدها.

Implementation notes

تُسجَّل الأزمنة لتحديد نافذة الصيانة.

Testing requirements

php artisan test --compact كاملًا على قاعدة البروفة، وفحوص يدوية لصفحات المسار.

Acceptance criteria

البروفة تمر كاملة دون تدخل يدوي، وزمنها معروف، والتراجع مجرَّب مرة واحدة على الأقل.

تشغيل RolesAndPermissionsSeeder، أو تخطي --dry-run.

## Role and goal
You are preparing and supporting Task 28 of the HC Tracking proposal-lifecycle correction plan: QA, full regression and UAT for the corrected story. You prepare the evidence for the Go/No-Go decision at CP6:
- the results of the automated quality gates;
- a test-gap audit against the Definition of Done;
- UAT scripts for each persona;
- concurrency, penetration, accessibility and RTL checklists;
- a defect log;
- a QA report with a recommendation.

You do not fix application code in this session. A failing check becomes a defect for the task that owns it. Human testers run UAT on a staging environment with their own HR accounts. You never log in as anyone, never handle passwords, and never run anything against production. The goal is proof that the whole story works for every role, not only for Super Admin and not only on the happy path:
- a project starts as a draft with no dates;
- concept note → internal review → submitted to the donor;
- proposal → review → submitted;
- donor approval fixes the dates and activates the projects;
- one agreement → an auto-generated transfer record (amount, `fees`, exchange rate completed by Finance) → aggregated donor reports for a chosen period;
- MEAL: library → logframe → per-centre targets → monthly reports generated at activation → monthly report → validation → Monthly Matrix;
- every movement on a project, proposal or report reaches MEAL and General Management (Task 21 event catalog).
